final_candidates.decision_summary: G170 is in the FAD-binding region of the catalytic domain; glycine-to-alanine substitution disrupts backbone flexibility critical for FAD coordination, likely abolishing electron transfer.

W165 is a conserved tryptophan adjacent to the FAD-binding poly-glutamate stretch; tryptophan likely stacks with the FAD isoalloxazine ring, and alanine substitution would disrupt FAD binding essential for catalysis.

D163 is a conserved aspartate in the catalytic core near the FAD-binding site; removal of the carboxylate side chain likely disrupts proton relay or substrate coordination required for hydride transfer.

stop_reason.detail: After position verification eliminated most initial candidates, three valid mutations in the FAD-binding/catalytic region were identified as the strongest loss-of-function candidates; further iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve confidence.

history.rationale: R594 is in the C-terminal regulatory/domain region; arginine-to-alanine may disrupt inter-domain interactions or substrate channeling required for activity.
